analysis_plan.contrast: control minus treated rate, with a repository-clustered bootstrap interval
analysis_plan.decision_rule: If the control arm rate is much lower than the treated arm rate, the strict rule discriminates and the RQ2 finding stands as an oracle-masking result. If the two arms are similar, RQ2 is reworded from 'a masking mechanism is observed in solved P2/P3 tasks' to 'the current rule does not single out P2/P3 tasks', and the rule is reported as a frame-dependent diagnostic.
analysis_plan.primary: strict masking rate in each arm, with Wilson two-sided 95% intervals
sensitivities: each conjunct reported separately per arm

counts.control_pool: benchmark-solved P0/P1 rows in the 480-task frame

design.goal: Test the discriminant validity of the RQ2 strict masking rule by running the same two-phase blind instrument on benchmark-solved P0/P1 tasks that are matched to the 12 benchmark-solved P2/P3 tasks.

matching.distance_variable: number of frozen public test runs that resolved the task

design.strict_rule: masked = oracle_alternative_fix_exists == yes AND available_evidence_unique_in_hindsight == no
design.why_needed: The second conjunct is close to the P2 definition, so a high rate on a P2/P3 selection may reflect the selection frame rather than a benchmark property.
design.within_panel_comparison: Both arms are labelled by the same new panel in one blinded worklist, so an arm difference cannot be explained by a panel effect. Re-labelling the 12 treated rows also gives an independent replication of the frozen 12/12.

label_freeze: This panel is a post-hoc diagnostic; it never edits the frozen repo480_available_v1 labels or the frozen RQ2 analysis.
phase2_gate: Phase 2 packages are built only after both Phase 1 returns are preserved and self-checked; each Phase 2 package reveals the oracle and that reviewer's own locked Phase 1 judgment, never the peer's.
